item.title: Jess Dillard-Wright
item.description: Jess is a white, fat, queer, genderqueer, feminist, antiracist, abolitionist, nurse dissident, activist-scholar. Dillard-Wright is associate professor and associate dean of equity and inclusion at the Elaine Marieb College of Nursing, University of Massachusetts Amherst, a Fellow of the American Academy of Nursing, and co-editor-in-chief of Nursing Philosophy. Her/their scholarship attends to ideas in nursing, working the intersections where feminism, nursing, and activism interact, from queer nursing histories and radical imagination to posthuman and new materialist care ethics. A founding member of the Nursology Theory Collective and co-organizer of Nursing Mutual Aid, she/they co-edited Nursing a Radical Imagination (Routledge, 2022) and remain a tentacle of the Compost Collaborative.

item.title: Jane Hopkins-Walsh
item.description: Jane is a white, bilingual, cis, hetero woman who works as a pediatric nurse practitioner in Boston, Massachusetts, USA. She holds a PhD from the Boston College Connell School of Nursing (2023) and completed a postdoctoral fellowship in nursing at Université Laval, Québec (2024–2025). In clinical practice at Boston Children’s Hospital Primary Care at Longwood since 1986, she is interested in the intersection of health and people in global mobility contexts. Her doctoral research examined patterning within stories about important people and events in the lives of emerging adults, ages 18–22, who have im/migrated from Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador. She co-edited Nursing a Radical Imagination (Routledge, 2022) and writes on critical posthumanist nursing.

item.title: Brandon Blaine Brown
item.description: Brandon is a white, cis, queer and newly middle class man. A registered nurse (MSN, RN-BC, CNL), he earned his B.S. in Nursing from Andrews University and a Master’s in Nursing Education from Norwich University. He is a Clinical Assistant Professor in the Department of Nursing at the University of Vermont, where he has taught since 2016, and practices in post-surgical and trauma care at the University of Vermont Medical Center, alongside doctoral study in education (EdD) at UVM. Brandon co-edited Nursing a Radical Imagination (Routledge, 2022) and writes at the intersection of nursing philosophy, posthumanism, and planetary health.

item.title: Eva Willis
item.description: Eva is white, cis, hetero woman from the countryside. A registered nurse and sociologist, she trained as a nurse in Germany and has practised in both German and British healthcare systems. She holds a BA in Social Sciences from the University of Kassel and an MSc in Sociology and Global Change from the University of Edinburgh. After a research post at Charité’s Institute of Clinical Nursing Science in Berlin, she is now a PhD candidate researching and teaching in the sociology of health and healthcare at the University of Siegen. Her PhD explores organisational knowledge embodied in nursing praxis and how the micropolitics of nursing affect patient care. Eva has two dogs and is committed to improving animal welfare.

item.title: Jamie B. Smith
item.description:
Jamie B Smith is a white, cis, queer newly middle class man. He brings nursing practice, institutional ethnography and critical posthuman philosophy to the Compost Collaborative’s shared work on care, power and more-than-human relations.

With fellow members, he co-authored Critical Posthuman Nursing Care and Mattering: Per/forming nursing philosophy in the Chthulucene. For his wider research, publications, consultancy and speaking, visit his personal website.

item.title: Christian Tedjasukmana
item.description:
Christian Tedjasukmana (he/him) RN, BSN, MFA is a nurse, artist, and designer based in the USA. Christian melds nursing and art together; his work calls attention to current myopic healthcare practices that contribute to climate change and negatively impact health. His public work includes the mural The Assimilation of Emmanuel, part of Burlington City Arts’ 4 x 8 Mural Project on race and belonging.

Selected works

  • Metastatic growth: The healthcare industry’s increasing contribution to the plasticene — in Nursing a Radical Imagination (Routledge, 2022)
  • Notes on [post]human nursing: What It MIGHT Be, What it is Not — Nursing Inquiry (2023)
  • Mattering: Per/forming nursing philosophy in the Chthulucene — Nursing Philosophy (2023, with the collective)

item.title: Annie-Claude Laurin
item.description: Annie-Claude Laurin, Inf., Ph.D., is an Assistant Professor (professeure adjointe) in the Faculté des sciences infirmières at Université Laval, Québec, Canada, and a researcher at the Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec. An intensive care nurse at the CHU de Québec–Université Laval since 2016, she completed her doctorate at Laval with SSHRC funding, studying nurses’ lived experience and actions in contexts of acharnement thérapeutique: perceived aggressive and futile treatment at the end of life in the intensive care unit. She is interested in the philosophical, social, and political structures which sustain this culture of death denial, in care and relational ethics, epistemic injustice, and nurses’ moral agency and resistance.

item.title: Patrick Martin
item.description:
Patrick Martin is a professor (professeur) in the Faculté des sciences infirmières at Université Laval, Québec, Canada. His work brings political philosophy into nursing: care ethics and democratic institutions, anarchism, epistemic injustice, and nurses’ resistance. He co-authored the collective’s imperative for critical posthuman research in nursing and appears in the Solidarity videos. In 2025 the Fondation de l’IUCPQ funded his study of LGBTQ2S+ nurses’ experiences of caring for LGBTQ2S+ patients.

Photo and full bio to come — this profile was rebuilt from verified public sources during the site migration; Patrick will expand it.

item.title: Kieran Sheehan
item.description: Kieran Sheehan is a movement artist and movement director who has worked for over twenty years across dance, theatre and opera, with credits including the Royal Shakespeare Company, Glyndebourne, the National Theatre and Opera North. His doctorate (EdD, St Mary’s University Twickenham, 2022) researched professional identities through intuitive movement — posthuman, diffractive video wonderings, the form behind his piece for the collective, Constantly Becoming With (2022). Formerly Acting Principal of the Academy of Live and Recorded Arts, he is now Co-director and Artistic Developer of Everyone Here, the Arts Council England-funded Creative People and Places programme for West Cumbria, where he leads the Jury for Joy — the UK’s first long-term citizens’ jury on creativity, featured by the UK Government’s Policy Lab.

item.title: About us
item.description:
We are an international collective of nurses, artists, critical theorists and anti-fascists. Nursing brings us together; it does not set the limits of what we can make or question.

What grows here

We work with critical posthumanism and feminist new materialism to ask how care takes shape between people, institutions, technologies and other living beings. Queer, feminist, abolitionist and anti-fascist thought runs through our writing, conversations and creative work.

Our projects include books, journal collaborations, movement, film and experiments in noticing. The collective bibliography gathers work by members; activities records the places where we meet, speak and make things together.

item.title: Activities
item.description:

IPONS 28th International Nursing Philosophy Conference — UC Irvine, 22–24 July 2026. The programme brought together Borderlands, camp and crip futures, with contributions from collective members. Read the conference note.

2025

“Imaginative archives for a more radical nursing future” — Jane, Annie-Claude and Patrick at the joint conference of the Canadian Society for the History of Medicine and the Canadian Association for the History of Nursing, Toronto, May 2025. The companion article is in Witness.

item.title: Annie-Claude joins the professoriate
item.description:
Université Laval welcomed Annie-Claude Laurin as a professeure assistante in its Faculté des sciences infirmières on 27 August 2025.

The announcement describes her intensive-care nursing experience and her research on ethics, epistemic injustice and nurses’ moral agency, including the political and philosophical dimensions of advanced nursing practice.

Read Laval’s appointment announcement, or meet Annie-Claude and explore her work with the collective.

item.title: Compost at IPONS 2026
item.description:
The 28th International Nursing Philosophy Conference met at UC Irvine and online on 22–24 July 2026. Its theme was Listening and Speaking Otherwise: Encounters at the Edge of Nursing and Philosophy. Jess co-chaired with Miriam Bender.

Seven members were represented on the programme. Jane facilitated Nursing the Borderlands, with Annie-Claude, Brandon and Eva. Jamie and Jess held the invited conversation Camp and the Politics of Seriousness in Nursing and Health Philosophy. Jamie also facilitated Camp, Professionalism, and Performative Critique, which included Abstractification in nursing education, co-authored by Tue-Chieu Mai and Patrick. Jamie joined Thinking the Event of Nursing. Jess facilitated Nursing Crip Futures.

item.title: Funding for LGBTQ2S+ nursing research
item.description:
On 5 February 2025, Université Laval announced a grant of CAD $14,000 from the Fondation de l’Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec for Patrick Martin’s research.

The project explores the experiences of LGBTQ2S+ nurses caring for LGBTQ2S+ patients. It brings questions of care, sexuality and gender into nursing research.

Read Laval’s funding announcement, or meet Patrick and find his writing on care ethics and nurse resistance.

item.title: Our position statement
item.description:
This consideration of our own roots speaks broadly and specifically to our position in the world; it is not exhaustive and will change. We place it here to begin to become accountable for our position and to make the power relations perceptible that make our worlds.

We believe this is especially important because the people and places we come from are not innocent. Not only do we speak about our privileges. We also speak about the limitations of our position and our perspective.

item.title: Projects
item.description:
Our ongoing collaborations and creative work live here. For citations, visit Published works; for conferences, panels and workshops, visit Activities.

Nursing a Radical Imagination

Examining the historical context of healthcare whilst focusing on building a more just, equitable world, this book proposes a radical imagination for nursing and presents possibilities for speculative futures embracing queer, feminist, posthuman, and abolitionist frames. Edited by Jess Dillard-Wright, Jane Hopkins-Walsh and Brandon Blaine Brown (Routledge, 2022). In the Journal of Advanced Nursing, Mick McKeown urged nurses to “read and act on the text”. item.title: Solidarity is a nursing intervention
item.description: During the hardest stretch of the pandemic we said it to camera, in two languages, from three countries: solidarity is a nursing intervention.

item.title: The imperative for critical posthuman research in nursing
item.description:
The full text of the imperative is being composted — it will fruit here soon.

In the meantime, the argument grows across our published work, including Notes on [post]human nursing: What It MIGHT Be, What it is Not (Nursing Inquiry, 2023) and Mattering: Per/forming nursing philosophy in the Chthulucene (Nursing Philosophy, 2023).
